post_mortality_remarriage.name: Remarriage After the Mortality
post_mortality_remarriage.observation: Widows and widowers remarry within months of the great mortality, and the next years bring more weddings and christenings than anyone remembers.

vacant_holding_migration.name: Filling the Empty Holdings
vacant_holding_migration.observation: Families leave poor hill farms to take up good land and town houses left empty by the dead.

decennial_household_registers.name: Ten-Yearly Household Registers
decennial_household_registers.observation: Village heads renew the household registers every ten years, listing each member, their age and their land.
decennial_household_registers.ability_reason: Every household in the realm is on a register renewed each decade, so tax, labour service and relief follow real numbers.
decennial_household_registers.social_consequence: Families cannot move without leaving the register, and village heads grow powerful over who is listed and how.

free_citizenship_grants.name: Free Citizenship Grants
free_citizenship_grants.observation: Towns emptied by the mortality grant citizenship without a fee to any incomer who will take up and repair an empty house.

wage_seeking_migration.name: Wage-Seeking Migration
wage_seeking_migration.observation: Labourers walk away from their home estates to wherever the pay is best, and lords cannot hold them.
wage_seeking_migration.social_consequence: Lords pass laws fixing wages and binding workers to their parishes, and the roads fill with men the law calls vagrants.

town_quarter_house_lists.name: Quarter House Lists
town_quarter_house_lists.observation: Each quarter of the town keeps a book listing its residents house by house, renewed at each quarter day.

public_dowry_fund.name: Public Dowry Fund
public_dowry_fund.observation: Fathers deposit a sum with the town fund at a daughter's birth, and it pays out many times over when she marries.

household_wealth_census.name: Household Wealth Census
household_wealth_census.observation: Every household declares each person, hearth, field, beast and debt, and clerks write it into great books for the tax.
household_wealth_census.ability_reason: The state knows every person and every asset in its territory, and tax falls where the wealth really is.
household_wealth_census.social_consequence: Households understate their wealth and hide their sons, and neighbours denounce one another to the assessors.

dowry_caps.name: Dowry Caps
dowry_caps.observation: The law caps the size of dowries, so more daughters of middling families can afford to marry.

census_age_recording.name: Ages in the Census
census_age_recording.observation: The census clerks write down each child's age, so the town knows how many will come of age for service and taxes.

registered_foundling_hospital.name: Registered Foundling Hospital
registered_foundling_hospital.observation: The foundling hospital writes each child taken in into a register and keeps a token left with it, so a mother may one day reclaim her child.
registered_foundling_hospital.ability_reason: Abandoned infants are taken in with a written record, so a mother can reclaim her child and the town can count what it loses.
registered_foundling_hospital.social_consequence: The token cabinet fills with pleading notes; most infants still die in their first year, but the town feels it has done its part.

health_office_death_registers.name: Death Registers
health_office_death_registers.observation: The health office writes down every death in the town with the person's age and the cause named by the physician.

foundling_wet_nurses.name: Foundling Wet-Nurses
foundling_wet_nurses.observation: The foundling hospital pays country women to suckle its infants in their own cottages.

town_orphanage.name: Town Orphanage
town_orphanage.observation: The town's orphanage raises fatherless children, teaches them letters and binds them apprentice at twelve.

women_refuge_houses.name: Women's Refuge Houses
women_refuge_houses.observation: Refuge houses take in women leaving the street trade, and give them work and, for some, a dowry.

pestilence_orphan_lists.name: Plague Orphan Lists
pestilence_orphan_lists.observation: After each outbreak the parish lists the orphans and widows the plague has left, and relief is paid by the list.

lineage_genealogy_books.name: Lineage Books
lineage_genealogy_books.observation: Clans reprint their lineage books each generation, adding every son born, and the book decides who shares in the ancestral hall.

expelled_community_refuge.name: Refuge for the Expelled
expelled_community_refuge.observation: A neighbouring realm takes in a community expelled from its homeland, under a charter guarding their quarter and their trades.
expelled_community_refuge.social_consequence: The newcomers' skills enrich the realm, while townsfolk resent their privileges and their separate ways.

emigrant_port_licences.name: Emigrant Licences
emigrant_port_licences.observation: Everyone sailing for the lands across the ocean must be licensed and counted at the port before boarding.

overseas_settler_colonies.name: Overseas Settler Colonies
overseas_settler_colonies.observation: Families cross the ocean with seed, tools and beasts and found farming colonies on newly found shores.
overseas_settler_colonies.ability_reason: Families take up land across the ocean, and the realm's people now grow on two shores.
overseas_settler_colonies.social_consequence: Colonists and native peoples meet over land, and the frontier becomes a place of raids, treaties and burning.

printed_midwife_manual.name: Printed Midwives' Manual
printed_midwife_manual.observation: A printed manual for midwives draws the child's positions in the womb and how to turn and deliver each.

contact_epidemic_records.name: Records of Contact Epidemics
contact_epidemic_records.observation: Missionaries write down how newly met peoples sicken and die by the village of pox and fevers that the newcomers barely notice.
contact_epidemic_records.ability_reason: The missions' registers show whole peoples dying of fevers and pox brought by strangers, and the pattern of crowd disease is written down.
contact_epidemic_records.social_consequence: The newcomers read the deaths as fate or as a warning; the survivors among the newly met peoples remember who brought the sickness.

shrine_vital_registers.name: Shrine Registers
shrine_vital_registers.observation: Every shrine keeps a register of each birth, marriage and burial among its people, and the book is checked at each visitation.
shrine_vital_registers.ability_reason: Every person's birth, marriage and burial is written down where they live, so age, descent and inheritance can be proved.

devotee_house_closure.name: Devotee Houses Closed
devotee_house_closure.observation: The houses of celibate devotees are closed, their lands sold, and their monks and nuns sent back into the world to marry and work.
devotee_house_closure.social_consequence: The faithful mourn the closed houses and the lost alms, and the poor lose the infirmaries the devotees kept.

marriage_dissolution_courts.name: Marriage Dissolution
marriage_dissolution_courts.observation: Marriage courts may dissolve a marriage for desertion or adultery, and the innocent party may marry again.

witnessed_marriage_rule.name: Witnessed Marriage
witnessed_marriage_rule.observation: A marriage is valid only when made in public before an officiant and two witnesses, and is written in the register.
witnessed_marriage_rule.ability_reason: Marriage requires a public ceremony before witnesses, so it can be proved, registered and inherited under.

mixed_descent_status.name: Mixed-Descent Standing
mixed_descent_status.observation: Children of settlers and native mothers are given their own legal standing, with rights below the settlers' and above the natives'.

postmortem_caesarean_rule.name: Postmortem Caesarean
postmortem_caesarean_rule.observation: When a mother dies in labour, the midwife or surgeon is bound to cut the child from her body at once.

weekly_mortality_bills.name: Weekly Bills of Mortality
weekly_mortality_bills.observation: Each week the capital prints the numbers of burials and christenings in every parish, with the causes of death.
weekly_mortality_bills.ability_reason: The capital sees plague coming in the weekly bills; merchants read them to flee early and the council to act.

living_mother_caesarean.name: Caesarean with a Living Mother
living_mother_caesarean.observation: A surgeon cuts a child from a living mother whose birth cannot proceed, and now and then both survive.

annual_soul_lists.name: Soul Lists
annual_soul_lists.observation: Each year the shrine keeper goes house to house and writes down every resident, servant and lodger.

headright_land_grants.name: Headright Grants
headright_land_grants.observation: Anyone who pays the passage of a settler across the ocean is granted a measure of land for each head brought.
headright_land_grants.social_consequence: Planters grow rich by shipping servants, and the servants themselves get no land.

secret_obstetric_forceps.name: Secret Forceps
secret_obstetric_forceps.observation: A family of man-midwives delivers stuck children with a hinged iron instrument they hide under the bedsheet and sell to no one.
secret_obstetric_forceps.social_consequence: The secret saves the family's clients and makes its fortune, while other mothers die of the same births.

soldier_marriage_limits.name: Soldiers' Marriage Limits
soldier_marriage_limits.observation: Only a few soldiers in each company may marry, and their wives and children follow the camp, washing and cooking for the regiment.

man_midwives.name: Man-Midwives
man_midwives.observation: Town families call a man-midwife with instruments to hard births that the midwife cannot deliver.
man_midwives.social_consequence: Midwives lose their best fees to the men, and some say the men use their hooks too soon.

ship_passenger_lists.name: Passenger Lists
ship_passenger_lists.observation: Every settlers' ship carries a list of passengers by name, age and trade, filed at both ends of the voyage.

childbed_death_counts.name: Childbed Deaths Counted
childbed_death_counts.observation: The bills count the deaths of mothers in childbed apart, and physicians see how many die and where.

strict_family_settlement.name: Strict Family Settlement
strict_family_settlement.observation: Great estates are settled on the eldest son and his eldest son after him, and none may sell or divide them.
strict_family_settlement.ability_reason: Great estates are tied to the eldest line for generations, and cannot be sold or divided.
strict_family_settlement.social_consequence: Younger sons and daughters take portions in cash and leave, and the land market stiffens.

burial_age_entries.name: Ages in the Burial Register
burial_age_entries.observation: The burial registers note the age of each person buried, and the clerk can see how old the town's dead are.

mortality_bill_arithmetic.name: Political Arithmetic
mortality_bill_arithmetic.observation: A merchant draws tables from years of the mortality bills and finds that births, deaths and the sexes follow steady proportions.
mortality_bill_arithmetic.ability_reason: Counting burials and christenings reveals regular laws of life and death, and the state can reckon its people from its records.

colonist_bride_passages.name: Colonist Brides
colonist_bride_passages.observation: Young women are shipped out with dowries from the crown to marry the settlers of the colonies.

large_family_tax_relief.name: Large Family Tax Relief
large_family_tax_relief.observation: Fathers of ten or more living children are freed from certain taxes.

country_wet_nursing.name: Country Wet-Nursing
country_wet_nursing.observation: Town mothers send their newborns to wet-nurses in the country and go back to the shop and the next pregnancy.
country_wet_nursing.social_consequence: Town infants sent to the country die in numbers their mothers never learn.

colonial_household_registers.name: Colonial Registers
colonial_household_registers.observation: Colonial governors register every household of settlers, servants and natives, with ranks written beside each name.

separate_wife_property.name: Wife's Separate Property
separate_wife_property.observation: Marriage contracts keep a wife's own property apart from her husband's, safe from his creditors.

populationist_policy.name: Populationist Policy
populationist_policy.observation: Ministers count people as the realm's wealth and reward marriage, large families and immigrants.

faith_refugee_edict.name: Faith Refugee Edict
faith_refugee_edict.observation: The ruler invites refugees of a faith proscribed abroad, with land, years free of tax and the right to their own worship.
faith_refugee_edict.ability_reason: Skilled refugees settle with land, tax years and their own worship, bringing trades the realm lacked.
faith_refugee_edict.social_consequence: Old subjects grumble at the newcomers' privileges, and the shrine keepers of the old faith call it an insult to the god.

tontine_annuities.name: Tontine
tontine_annuities.observation: Subscribers buy shares in a fund whose yearly payments are divided among those still alive, until the last survivor takes all.

register_life_table.name: Life Table
register_life_table.observation: A scholar reckons from a town's registers how many of a thousand born are still alive at each age.
register_life_table.ability_reason: The chance of dying at each age is written from a town's own registers, and annuities and pensions can be priced honestly.

vital_events_tax.name: Vital Events Tax
vital_events_tax.observation: A tax is charged on every birth, marriage and burial, and bachelors over twenty-five pay yearly.

birth_multiplier_estimates.name: Birth Multiplier
birth_multiplier_estimates.observation: The number of people in a province is estimated by multiplying its yearly births by a fixed number.

nominal_realm_census.name: Realm Census
nominal_realm_census.observation: On one set day every person in the realm is written down by name, age and household.
nominal_realm_census.ability_reason: For one set day every person in the realm is named and counted, and the state knows its full strength.
nominal_realm_census.social_consequence: Many fear the count means new taxes or a levy, and hide in the woods on census day.

birth_sex_ratio.name: Birth Sex Ratio
birth_sex_ratio.observation: Every year's registers show a few more boys than girls born, and scholars debate why.

post_plague_colonization.name: Resettling Plague Districts
post_plague_colonization.observation: The state brings colonists to farm districts that plague has emptied, with seed, beasts and tax-free years.

marriage_register_details.name: Marriage Register Details
marriage_register_details.observation: Marriage registers now record both partners' ages and birthplaces.

convict_transportation.name: Convict Transportation
convict_transportation.observation: Convicts are shipped to the overseas colonies to work out their sentences.
convict_transportation.social_consequence: Families never see their transported men again, and the colonists resent being made the realm's prison.

midwife_birth_returns.name: Midwives' Birth Returns
midwife_birth_returns.observation: Sworn midwives return to the clerk a count of every birth they attend, living and stillborn.

military_orphanage.name: Military Orphanage
military_orphanage.observation: A soldiers' orphanage raises the children of the regiments, and many of the boys enlist as drummers.

lodging_guest_registers.name: Lodging Registers
lodging_guest_registers.observation: Every inn and lodging-house must register each guest and stranger with the watch.

published_obstetric_forceps.name: Forceps Made Public
published_obstetric_forceps.observation: The hinged forceps are published and taught to midwives and surgeons, and every town has someone who can use them.
published_obstetric_forceps.ability_reason: Forceps are taught openly, and a stuck birth need no longer mean a dead mother or a crushed child.
published_obstetric_forceps.social_consequence: Clumsy hands use the forceps too often, and some mothers are torn who would have delivered alone.

national_foundling_hospital.name: National Foundling Hospital
national_foundling_hospital.observation: A national foundling hospital takes infants from every part of the realm, carried to it in baskets by carriers.
national_foundling_hospital.social_consequence: Carriers bring infants by the wagonload and many die on the road; the hospital is overwhelmed within a few years.

divine_order_population_treatise.name: Treatise on the Divine Order
divine_order_population_treatise.observation: A shrine scholar draws on the registers of many districts to show a steady order in births, marriages and deaths, and calls it the god's design.

actuarial_widows_fund.name: Widows' Fund
actuarial_widows_fund.observation: A fund for the widows of shrine keepers and teachers sets its payments by the life tables, and does not run dry.

lying_in_hospital.name: Lying-In Hospital
lying_in_hospital.observation: A hospital for poor mothers gives them a clean bed, a midwife and ten days' rest after the birth.
lying_in_hospital.social_consequence: Childbed fever sweeps the wards some winters, and the hospital becomes feared in its turn.

population_tables_office.name: Population Tables Office
population_tables_office.observation: A standing office receives each district's yearly report of births, deaths and numbers, and prints the tables for the realm.
population_tables_office.ability_reason: Every district reports its births, deaths and numbers each year, and the state follows its people's growth as it happens.

life_expectancy_tables.name: Expectation of Life
life_expectancy_tables.observation: Scholars reckon how many more years a person of each age may expect to live.

settler_doubling_observation.name: Settler Doubling
settler_doubling_observation.observation: Observers notice that the settler colonies double their numbers every generation, where the old country barely grows.

clandestine_marriage_ban.name: Secret Marriages Void
clandestine_marriage_ban.observation: Secret marriages are declared void; a couple needs a licence or banns and an entry in the register.
clandestine_marriage_ban.social_consequence: Young couples who cannot win their parents' consent can no longer marry in secret, and more stay single.

maternal_nursing_campaign.name: Mothers Nurse Their Own
maternal_nursing_campaign.observation: Physicians and writers urge mothers of every rank to nurse their own infants, and it becomes a fashion.

inoculation_mortality_reckoning.name: Inoculation Reckoned
inoculation_mortality_reckoning.observation: Scholars compare smallpox deaths among the inoculated and the uninoculated and publish the reckoning.

frontier_colonist_recruitment.name: Frontier Colonist Recruitment
frontier_colonist_recruitment.observation: State agents recruit farmers abroad for the empty frontier, promising free land, tax-free years and their own villages.
frontier_colonist_recruitment.ability_reason: The state fills its frontier with recruited colonists, who plough the steppe and hold it.
frontier_colonist_recruitment.social_consequence: The frontier peoples lose their pastures to the colonists' ploughs, and the old borderers resent the foreigners.

manikin_midwife_schools.name: Midwife Schools with a Manikin
manikin_midwife_schools.observation: A travelling instructress teaches village midwives with a life-size cloth mother and child, and the state pays their fees.

wet_nurse_bureau.name: Wet-Nurse Bureau
wet_nurse_bureau.observation: The city registers wet-nurses, checks their health and pays them through a bureau.

pauper_marriage_bar.name: Pauper Marriage Bar
pauper_marriage_bar.observation: Paupers who cannot show means are barred from marrying.
pauper_marriage_bar.social_consequence: Couples live together unwed and their children are born outside the law.

emigrant_recruiting_agents.name: Emigrant Agents
emigrant_recruiting_agents.observation: Agents travel the villages recruiting whole farming families for the lands across the ocean.

infant_death_causes.name: Infant Deaths by Cause
infant_death_causes.observation: Infant deaths are counted by cause and season, and summer fluxes are seen to kill most.

marital_birth_limitation.name: Deliberate Birth Limitation
marital_birth_limitation.observation: Couples stop having children after two or three, on purpose, and raise those better.
marital_birth_limitation.ability_reason: Couples who stop after two or three children feed and school them better, and mothers survive fewer childbeds.
marital_birth_limitation.social_consequence: Shrine keepers denounce the practice, and it spreads anyway, first among townsfolk and small proprietors.

secret_birth_house.name: Secret Birth House
secret_birth_house.observation: Unmarried mothers may deliver in a birth house without giving their names, and leave the child in care.

foundling_nurse_inspection.name: Foundling Nurse Inspection
foundling_nurse_inspection.observation: The foundling hospital counts its dead and sends inspectors to the country nurses.

decennial_apportionment_census.name: Apportionment Census
decennial_apportionment_census.observation: Every ten years the people are counted and the assembly's seats shared among the districts by head count.
decennial_apportionment_census.ability_reason: Seats in the assembly follow the head count every ten years, and the census becomes the ground of lawful power.

civil_vital_registration.name: Civil Registration
civil_vital_registration.observation: Town officials, not shrine keepers, register every birth, marriage and death, whatever a person's faith.
civil_vital_registration.ability_reason: Every birth, marriage and death is recorded by the state itself, for all its people alike.
civil_vital_registration.social_consequence: Shrine keepers lose their oldest duty and fees, and the devout call the civil registers an insult to the god.

civil_divorce.name: Civil Divorce
civil_divorce.observation: A couple may end their marriage by mutual consent before a civil officer.

population_pressure_treatise.name: Treatise on Population
population_pressure_treatise.observation: A treatise argues that numbers grow faster than food unless war, famine, disease or restraint check them.
population_pressure_treatise.ability_reason: Statesmen now weigh relief, marriage and food against the growth of numbers.
